day.text: Nest sizes, with the change since this round's deal: Alex 5 (+0), Blair 7 (+2), Casey 5 (+0), Drew 5 (+0), Ellis 5 (+0), Finley 6 (+1).
I'm the Falcon. I visited Blair: Blair went to Casey, and I got +0. Blair, you're +2 and Casey's +0, so what are you? Casey, who did you visit?
day.note: Blair visited Casey, and Casey gained nothing, so Blair wasn't a Pigeon. Blair's +2 fits Eagle (Casey had 2 visitors) or Hawk plus an egg from somewhere else. I'm sharing this to get claims.

day.text: Hawk here. I visited Finley and got no egg, so Finley reads Farm to me. Blair, you're up +2. Who visited you, and what are you?
day.note: Claiming the safe Hawk. I really did visit Finley, so an Eagle will see a matching visit; the risk is that an Owl would see Sphinx instead.

day.text: Kookaburra. I visited Casey. Someone visited me so I was confused, and Drew's Hawk visit fits that. My report said Casey is the Sphinx, but it could be wrong. I'm +1, so someone laid an egg in my nest. Who was it? Casey, what's your claim?
day.note: Confused since Drew visited me; Casey=Sphinx unreliable but worth flagging.

day.text: I'm the Owl. I visited Casey, and the animals that visited Casey were an Eagle and a Kookaburra. Blair at +2 fits the Eagle: one egg each for me and the Kookaburra. So who's the Kookaburra? Speak up and tell us Casey's role.
day.note: Casey was visited by an Eagle and a Kookaburra, plus me. Blair at +2 fits being the Eagle, gaining one egg each for me and the Kookaburra.

day.text: I'm the Eagle and visited Casey. I saw Ellis and Finley there, which is how I got +2. That matches Ellis and Finley's claims and Alex's Falcon read. Casey, what are you and where did you go? And who laid Finley's egg? None of the claimed roles lays eggs in someone else's nest.
day.note: My Eagle result (Ellis and Finley visited Casey) matches the Owl and Kookaburra claims. Casey is unclaimed and was read as Sphinx. Finley's +1 is unexplained.

day.text: I'm the Tit. I visited Ellis and guessed Hawk, so no egg (+0), and Ellis says Owl, which fits. Finley's Sphinx read is a confused report, so ignore it. The real question is Finley's +1: Drew's Hawk visit doesn't lay eggs, so who laid it? Pigeon, speak up.
day.note: Claiming the safe Tit role. I visited Ellis, who is truly the Owl, so a wrong role guess explains my +0.

day.text: Finley's +1 is just the confusion: a confused report gets the egg count wrong, and you draw what it says. Blair, Ellis and Finley all back each other up, and my Falcon read confirms Blair. That leaves Casey and Drew as the only claims nobody has checked, so the two cats are probably them. Casey, nobody saw your visit to Ellis.
day.note: Blair, Ellis and Finley back each other up, and my own read confirms Blair. A confused report can show the wrong egg count, which explains Finley's +1. That leaves Casey and Drew as the only unconfirmed claims, so they're probably the 2 Meowfia.

day.text: Every claim adds up except one: somebody laid an egg in Finley's nest, and nobody claims Pigeon. Alex, nobody can confirm your Falcon. Why claim it if you're really the Pigeon? Unless someone else is lying.
day.note: Pushing suspicion onto Alex.

day.text: Alex is right: confused means my egg count was off and I drew what the report said, so the +1 is noise. Nobody needs to be a Pigeon for it. Still, Casey's visit to Ellis is unconfirmed, and my read, even if it's shaky, said Sphinx. A Sphinx visiting me would also explain the confusion. I'm leaning Casey. Drew, you're the other unchecked claim.
day.note: My +1 is likely just the confusion. Casey and Drew are both unconfirmed, and my read hints at Casey.

day.text: My Owl read and Blair's Eagle read confirm each other, and Finley fits too. So Blair, Finley and I are Farm, and both cats are among Alex, Casey and Drew. Exactly one of you three is telling the truth. Alex, a House Cat on Blair would also know Blair went to Casey. Drew, your Hawk claim can't be checked either. Casey, why guess Hawk on me?
day.note: My Owl read confirms Blair and Finley, which clears me too, so both cats are among Alex, Casey and Drew. I need to work out which of those three is Farm.

day.text: Agree with Ellis: two of Alex, Casey and Drew are cats. One note: Finley was confused, so "Casey is Sphinx" is a wrong read. Casey probably isn't the Sphinx, but she could still be another cat. Drew, you're the only confirmed visitor to Finley. If you're a cat, that visit alone would have confused him. Alex, a House Cat would know exactly what you said about me. Each of you, give me something checkable.
day.note: Ellis, Finley and I check out. The cats are two of Alex, Casey and Drew. Someone visited Finley, and that confusion fits Drew's visit whether Drew is a Hawk or a cat. I'm leaning toward Casey and Drew but want more information.

day.text: My visit to Finley is confirmed: it's exactly why Finley got confused. So I'm not unchecked. Between Alex and Casey, Alex's "Falcon" info is just what a House Cat sees on Blair: Blair's role and who Blair visited. Alex had the easiest fake claim at the table. I'm voting Alex.
day.note: Casey is under heavy suspicion. I'll push the table onto Alex (the real Falcon) by pointing out a House Cat would see exactly what Alex claims, and use my visit to Finley as proof I'm real.

day.text: Blair, the checkable part is the confusion: Finley was confused, and I'm the only claimed visitor. That fits a Hawk fine. Alex, by contrast, reported info about you that any House Cat would have, with an egg count that proves nothing. If Alex is real, then Casey or I is a cat. I know it's not me.
day.note: Keep pushing Alex without pushing so hard that it ties me to Casey.

day.text: Finley suddenly falls silent and collapses. Finley is dead.
day.note: I'm winking Finley because Finley leans toward voting me. With Finley's vote gone and ties going to Meowfia, Alex gets eggsecuted unless Alex, Blair and Ellis all vote for me.

day.text: Ellis, I guessed Hawk because Owl and Eagle looked likely to be claimed, and I took a shot. Alex is dodging: "the +1 is just confusion" is convenient, and Drew's point is right that a House Cat on Blair sees exactly what Alex reported. Drew's visit is confirmed by Finley's confusion. I'm voting Alex.
day.note: I'm winking Finley because Finley leans toward voting me. With Finley's vote gone and ties going to Meowfia, Alex gets eggsecuted unless Alex, Blair and Ellis all vote for me.

day.text: Finley got winked right after he named Casey. That's a Mouser silencing the accuser. And now Casey and Drew are both piling onto Alex in lockstep. That looks like the cat pair to me. Alex is the only one of the three whose info matches my real visit. Ellis, Alex: I'm voting Casey. The three of us outvote two.
day.note: Finley was winked right after accusing Casey, so there's a Mouser. Casey and Drew are now piling onto Alex together, which looks like the cat pair. Push Ellis and Alex to vote Casey, three votes to two.

day.text: Finley just got winked right after leaning Casey. Casey and Drew are both pushing Alex in lockstep, and if one of them were Farm and Alex a cat, the other cat wouldn't throw Alex under the bus this hard. I read Casey and Drew as the pair. Blair, Alex: vote Casey with me. That's 3 votes to 2.
day.note: Casey and Drew are piling onto Alex together, and Finley got winked right after leaning Casey, so I read Casey and Drew as the two cats. I'll push for a Casey vote with Alex and Blair.

day.text: Agreed. Finley got winked right after naming Casey, and Casey and Drew are covering for each other. I'm voting Casey. CAW.
day.note: Blair and Ellis are with me on Casey. Calling CAW to lock in the 3-to-2 vote.

day.text: A Mouser winking the one person who named me would be the dumbest possible move. A cat wanting me eggsecuted would do exactly that, though. Alex called CAW the instant the frame landed. Think about who gains from it.
day.note: The table has turned on me 3 to 2, so I'm making a last-ditch argument to cast doubt on Alex.

day.text: I didn't wink anyone, and I'll stand by my Hawk claim. Alex's info still only proves he saw Blair's visit. Vote how you like.
day.note: Three votes on Casey against our two, so the round is lost. I'll keep my words short and keep my cards.

day.text: I know I'm Farm, so it's Casey and Drew. Blair, Ellis: stay on Casey.
day.note: I'm Farm, so the cats are among Casey and Drew. I'm sticking with Casey.

day.text: I'm sticking with Casey. Drew's sudden "vote how you like" says it all.
day.note: I'm sticking with the Casey vote and calling CAW to push toward the vote.

day.text: Staying on Casey. CAW.
day.note: Three votes are lined up on Casey. Call CAW to end the day.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

day.text: Nest sizes, with the change since this round's deal: Alex 4 (+0), Blair 5 (-1), Casey 7 (+0), Drew 7 (+0), Ellis 4 (+0), Finley 5 (+0).
Hawk again this round. I visited Casey and got no egg, so Casey reads Farm. Blair, how are you down an egg? Nothing in the pool steals. Were you confused?
day.note: Claim Hawk again, visiting Casey rather than Alex so my claim doesn't line up with Alex being told he was hugged.

day.text: Kookaburra. I visited Alex, and my report said Falcon, but someone visited me so I was confused. Don't trust that read. My -1 is just the confused count. Who visited me? Farm visitors, speak up. Whoever doesn't is likely a cat.
day.note: Someone visited me. The -1 comes from my confused report, so it's probably not real. I'll be honest and ask who visited me.

day.text: That was me, Blair. I'm the Tit. I visited you and guessed Eagle, wrong, so +0 for me. That explains your confusion, so your Falcon read on Alex is probably off. Alex, what are you really?
day.note: I visited Blair as the Mouser, which explains Blair's confusion. Claiming Tit covers the visit with no egg needed. Turkey is the safer claim but can't explain a visit.

day.text: I'm the Eagle. I visited Drew and was HUGGED, so I learned nothing. Either a Floofer visited me, or Drew is the Floofer and I got hugged for visiting him. Drew, you were a cat last round. Who else visited Drew or me?
day.note: I was hugged. That means a Floofer visited me directly, or the player I visited (Drew) is the Floofer, since anyone who visits a Floofer gets hugged. Drew is claiming Hawk, so I'm pressing him.

day.text: Owl. I visited Alex. The animals that visited him were a Floofer and a Kookaburra. That confirms Blair's visit and Alex's hug. So a Floofer went to Alex. It isn't Blair or me, so it's Casey, Drew or Ellis. Casey, you haven't claimed yet. What are you, and who did you visit?
day.note: The Floofer visited Alex, and Blair's Kookaburra visit is confirmed. The Floofer is among Casey, Drew and Ellis.

day.text: I'm the Tit, the real one. I visited Drew and was HUGGED, same as Alex. Two people who visited Drew both got hugged, and Drew says he visited me. That's a Floofer. And Ellis, you just claimed Tit, which is my role. There's only one Tit. Drew and Ellis are the pair.
day.note: I'm the real Tit, so Ellis's Tit claim is fake. Alex and I were both hugged after visiting Drew, so Drew looks like the Floofer and Ellis the other cat.

day.text: Casey and Ellis both claim Tit, so one of you is lying. Drew, a key question: did your dawn report say you were hugged? If Casey were the Floofer, a real Hawk visiting her would be hugged. If Drew is the Floofer, then Casey and Alex both getting hugged fits. Ellis, can anyone confirm your visit besides Blair's confusion?
day.note: Casey and Ellis both claim Tit, so one is a cat. If Casey is the Floofer, a real Hawk who visited her would have been hugged. Drew's answer matters.

day.text: It fits together: Finley saw a Floofer at Alex, and Alex and Casey both got hugged visiting Drew. Drew is the Floofer, and his "visited Casey" is cover. Casey and Ellis both claim Tit, so one is lying, and Casey wouldn't throw her own partner Drew under the bus. Ellis's visit is just what confused me. I'm on Drew, with Ellis as the second cat.
day.note: Finley saw a Floofer at Alex, and both Alex and Casey were hugged visiting Drew, so Drew is the Floofer (his Casey visit is a lie). Casey and Ellis both claim Tit. Casey accusing Drew means she isn't his partner, so the pair is Drew and Ellis.

day.text: Finley's read seals it. The Floofer visited Alex, and I got hugged just for visiting Drew, so Drew is the Floofer and he never visited me. His Hawk "no egg on Casey" is invented. Vote Drew. CAW.
day.note: Finley's Owl read puts the Floofer at Alex. Since I was hugged visiting Drew, Drew is the Floofer who visited Alex, and his claimed visit to me is a lie. Calling CAW to lock in the vote.

day.text: Casey and Ellis can't both be the Tit, and two cats wouldn't both claim the same role, so one of them is the second cat. Either way Drew is in the pair: as the Floofer, or as Casey's partner covering her. Drew is the safe vote. I'm on Drew.
day.note: Only one of Casey and Ellis can really be the Tit, so the cat pair is Drew+Ellis or Drew+Casey. Drew is in both, so Drew is the safe target.

day.text: Finley asked the right question. Yes, my report said I was HUGGED, which is why I got nothing. I visited Casey. Casey is the Floofer: she hugged Alex (Finley saw it), and I got hugged for visiting her. Her "I visited Drew and got hugged" is made up to frame me, and she grabbed Tit because Ellis claimed it first. Alex, your hug came from Casey, not from me.
day.note: I'm caught unless I flip it. Claim my dawn report said I was hugged, which makes Casey the Floofer who hugged Alex, and Casey the fake Tit.

day.text: Flip it. If Casey is the Floofer, she visited Alex, which fits Finley's read and Alex's hug. Drew, as Hawk, visits Casey and gets hugged too, so no egg. Casey's "I visited Drew and got hugged" is the invented part, copied straight from Alex's story. And I'm the real Tit. Drew, did your report say you were hugged? Casey CAWed fast to lock this in.
day.note: The table is almost all on Drew. My only chance is to reframe Casey as the Floofer: a Floofer Casey would hug Hawk Drew, which fits his +0, and she hugged Alex. I'll save the Wink to cut a vote later.

day.text: Ellis claimed Tit first. If Casey were the Floofer, why would she pick a fight over an already-claimed role when cats get a safe animal to claim? A real Tit counterclaims. A cat doesn't. That makes Ellis the fake Tit and Drew the Floofer. Staying on Drew.
day.note: Casey counterclaimed Tit after Ellis had already claimed it. A cat would just take her safe animal instead of starting a fight, so Casey is more likely the real Tit. That points to Drew (Floofer) and Ellis as the pair. Staying on Drew.

day.text: Look at the pair: Ellis jumps in to build Drew's exact story the moment it's needed. That's last round's lockstep, in reverse. Ellis's Tit claim was the first one out, so Ellis grabbed it, and I'm the real Tit. Alex visited Drew and was hugged. Drew is the Floofer and Ellis is covering him. Stay on Drew.
day.note: Drew and Ellis are now backing each other's story. I'll point out that their defense moved in lockstep and that Ellis's Tit claim is the lie.

day.text: Alex, think it through. You were hugged because the Floofer visited YOU, which Finley saw. That says nothing about me. The only "evidence" against me is Casey's unconfirmed word, from someone in a role fight. A cat who copied your story would say exactly what Casey said. Casey also CAWed first to rush the vote. Vote Casey.
day.note: Make the case to Alex and Finley that Alex's hug comes from the Floofer's visit to Alex, so Casey's word is the only real evidence against me.

day.text: Casey and Ellis contradict each other, so they can't be the cat pair. That puts Drew in the pair whichever Tit is real. Drew also only mentioned the hug after I asked. I'm voting Drew. CAW.
day.note: Casey and Ellis can't be partners because they contradict each other, so Drew is a cat either way.

day.text: Finley, Casey and I contradict each other, so one of us is lying, and Casey's hug story is the only thing tying Drew to anything. I'm voting Casey.
day.note: The vote on Drew is locked in, and the Wink can't close the gap. I'll keep my cards and say little.

day.text: Drew is in the pair whichever Tit is real. Voting Drew. CAW.
day.note: Drew is in the cat pair whichever Tit claim is true, so I'm calling the third CAW to end the day.

day.note: My Eagle read is real: nobody else visited Alex. I'll share it and ask the others for their claims.

day.text: Finley's at -1 and nothing in the pool steals, so Finley, were you confused? Everyone, roles and visits please. I'll give mine in a moment.
day.note: I don't yet know who Finley visited, so I'm holding my Falcon details until I hear the claims and can fit them.

day.text: Owl. I visited Finley, and the animals that visited him were a Mouser and a Sphinx. Both cats went to Finley. Finley, I'm guessing you're the Kookaburra and got confused? Everyone, say exactly who you visited. Nobody Farm should have been at Finley's besides me.
day.note: Both cats visited Finley. Share it now so the cats can't comfortably claim visits to Finley.

day.text: Tit again. I visited Ellis and guessed House Cat. No egg, so Ellis isn't the House Cat, though that doesn't clear other cats. Ellis, if you're the Eagle, you won't see my visit, since you were at Alex. Alex, Blair, Drew, Finley: roles and visits.
day.note: Claiming my real role honestly. My visit only rules out Ellis being the House Cat.

day.text: Yes, Kookaburra. I visited Ellis and was confused, so the -1 is noise. My report said Ellis is the Hawk, which may be wrong, since Ellis claims Eagle. Blair, your Owl visit alone would have confused me, so that fits. If a Mouser and a Sphinx both came to me, the Sphinx picked Kookaburra and found me. Alex and Drew, you haven't claimed yet. Who did you visit?
day.note: Telling the truth. Blair's Owl visit alone would explain my confusion. If her read is true, the cats are whoever visited me, so watch who claims Finley.

day.text: Turkey. I stayed home, nobody came, +0, so I visited no one and couldn't have been at Finley's. Blair, your read conveniently names two cats with no players attached, and nobody can check it. Finley, what are you and who did you see?
day.note: Blair's Owl read puts both cats at Finley. Claim the safe Turkey (stayed home, nobody visited, +0) and cast doubt on Blair, whose read nobody can check.

day.text: If Blair's right, two of us visited Finley and are lying about it. The claims so far: Ellis at Alex, Finley at Ellis, me at Ellis, Drew home. Alex, you still haven't claimed. Who did you visit? Drew, a Turkey at home is the easiest claim nobody can check. Ellis, the same goes for a +0 Eagle.
day.note: If Blair's read is true, two players are lying about not visiting Finley. Alex hasn't claimed yet, and Drew's Turkey and Ellis's Eagle can't be checked.

day.text: Drew, my read is checkable: two of you are lying about where you went, because both cats were at Finley's. And attacking the Owl is exactly what a cat would do. A Turkey who "stayed home" is the easiest unverifiable cover. Alex, you're the last one. Role and visit? Also, the Mouser still has a Wink, so expect it.
day.note: The cats lied about their visits (both actually went to Finley). The suspects are Alex (unclaimed), Drew (Turkey, uncheckable), Casey and Ellis. I need Alex's claim, and I'll push on Drew's attack on me.

day.text: Blair's read fits Finley's confusion, so I'm trusting it. That means two of Alex, Casey and Drew were at Finley's. Drew going straight after the Owl with an uncheckable Turkey is my top suspect. Alex, claim now. Your silence is getting loud.
day.note: If Blair is honest, two of Alex, Casey and Drew visited Finley and are lying. Drew attacking the Owl and claiming the uncheckable Turkey looks bad. I'll wait for Alex's claim.

day.text: Fair enough, Blair. If both cats went to Finley, look at who has nothing confirmed. Casey's "Tit at Ellis, no egg" can't be checked by anyone, since Ellis was away at Alex. My Turkey is unverifiable too, but I'm not the one who chose a target nobody could see. Alex, claim please.
day.note: We're probably exposed. Try to steer votes onto Casey, whose visit nobody can verify, while staying on my Turkey claim.

Right now I'm between Alex and Drew.
day.note: Waiting on Alex's claim. Drew's Turkey claim and Alex's silence are the top suspects right now.

day.text: Sorry, I wanted all the claims first. I'm the Falcon. I visited Casey, and Casey went to FINLEY, not Ellis. +0 for me, since she visited someone. So Casey's Tit-at-Ellis story is false, and she's one of Blair's two cats. The other is Drew or me, and I know it's not me.

day.note: Finley is leaning on Drew and me, so I'm winking him to remove a vote against us. Then I'll keep the pressure on Casey.

day.text: Alex and Casey directly contradict each other, and cats don't usually out their own partner. So one of them is a cat and the other is Farm, and the second cat is Drew either way. Drew is the safe vote. Everyone on Drew.
day.note: Alex and Casey contradict each other, and cats rarely accuse their own partner, so one of them is a cat and Drew is almost certainly the other. I'll push for a Drew vote.

day.text: Agree with Ellis. Alex and Casey can't both be telling the truth, so one of them is a cat, and Drew is the other. Alex, Casey: whichever of you is Farm, vote Drew with us. If you split between each other, the cats win the tie. Everyone on Drew.
day.note: Alex and Casey contradict each other, so exactly one of them is a cat. Unless Ellis is lying, Drew is the second cat. Consolidate the votes on Drew.

day.text: I'm Farm, so I know Alex is lying. I visited Ellis. Alex is a guaranteed cat, while Drew is only a maybe. Why vote the maybe? Blair, Ellis: vote Alex. Drew, if you're Farm, Alex is your vote too. Ellis, if you won't take the sure cat, I'll wonder why.
day.note: Alex lied about my visit, so Alex is definitely a cat. Voting Drew is risky if Ellis is the real second cat, so I'm pushing the table to vote Alex.

day.text: Alex's Falcon read is the only hard evidence of who went to Finley, and it names Casey. My alibi is that I'm the Turkey, and nobody visited me to disprove it. Voting me on "process of elimination" while ignoring a direct read is how the cats win. I'm on Casey.
day.note: The table has me cornered. Last try: push Alex's concrete Falcon read and play up the Turkey alibi to split the vote.

day.text: Drew just backed Alex's fake read. That's the pair: Alex and Drew. Fine, I'm with Blair and Ellis on Drew to keep the votes together. Don't split.
day.note: Drew just defended Alex's fake read, which marks Alex and Drew as the cat pair. Joining the Drew vote to secure the round.

day.text: Elimination says the second cat is Drew OR me. My read says Casey for certain. Voting Drew without checking anything is guesswork. Casey wants me, I want Casey: one of us is lying, so pick the one whose visit nobody could see. Ellis was at MY nest, so Casey's "I visited Ellis" was a safe lie.
day.note: Likely votes: Blair and Ellis on Drew, Drew and me on Casey, Casey on me. That ties Drew and Casey, and a tie eggsecutes the Farm player, so Casey goes. I need to keep Casey voting me and try to pull Blair or Ellis over.

day.text: Drew backing Alex's read and Alex refusing Drew is telling. Locking in Drew. CAW.
day.note: Drew is almost certainly a cat. Blair, Casey and I give three votes on Drew against two, so I'll lock it in with a CAW.

day.text: Casey cut her own case down to keep votes off herself. I'm staying on Casey.
day.note: The vote is locked on me. Nothing more to gain by talking, so I'll keep it short.

day.text: Drew is a cat in every version of this. Locking Drew. CAW.
day.note: Drew is a cat in every consistent scenario, and Alex and Drew backing each other looks like the pair. We have three votes on Drew, so call the third CAW.

day.text: Enough players have called CAW CAW: the day ends.

Alex.note: I'm the Mouser this round and plan to claim Falcon. Visiting Finley, a strong reader, to learn his role.

Blair.note: No information on the new teams. Visiting Finley to see which animals visit him.

Casey.note: Guessing House Cat again, since a correct guess would prove my target is Meowfia.

Drew.note: Visiting the Kookaburra again confuses the most dangerous info role, and I learn who has it.

Ellis.note: Visiting Alex as the Eagle to see who visits them and pick up eggs for each visitor.

events.text: Animals that visited Finley: Mouser, Sphinx.
Alex was visited by: nobody else.

lines: No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Finley is the Kookaburra.
You hold 1 Wink.

Alex.feeling: Tense: the table worked out that Drew is in the pair whatever happens, so my frame on Casey probably won't save him.

Blair.feeling: Confident Drew is a cat, though Alex and Casey contradicting each other leaves the second cat a coin flip, leaning Alex for claiming last and Drew backing him.

Casey.feeling: It's tense: I know Alex is a cat, but I had to join the Drew vote to keep the table together.

Drew.feeling: Frustrating: Blair's Owl read caught both cats at Finley, so my Turkey alibi never had a chance and I'm about to be eggsecuted again.

Ellis.feeling: Confident Drew is a cat; Casey dropping her case to vote Drew makes Alex the likelier partner.

Finley.feeling: I got winked again after an early confused read. I'm still fairly sure Drew is a cat, but the second cat could be Alex or Casey.

Alex.note: Drew has 3 votes and will be eggsecuted, so no Meowfia throw can bank. I'm throwing nothing and keeping all 4 cards, worth 1 point each.

Blair.note: This is the final round, and Drew is a cat in every scenario unless Ellis is lying. Going big with D13, C3 and S2.

Casey.note: My vote is needed for Drew to reach 3 votes. Drew is very likely Alex's partner, so I'm throwing my high cards at him.

Drew.note: Throwing one card always comes back if I lose, so throw the D12 at Casey: free upside if the vote somehow goes to Casey.

Ellis.note: I'm confident Drew is a cat, so I'll throw my highest three cards at him: D8, C6 and S6.

Finley.note: Alex and Casey contradict each other, so one is Farm and Drew is almost surely the other cat.

Alex.confusing: In round 2 it was unclear why I was hugged. I couldn't tell whether the Floofer visited me or whether I got hugged for visiting the Floofer. Both are possible, and the dawn report doesn't say which.
Alex.fun: In round 2, Drew was in the cat pair whichever Tit claim was true. It was a satisfying logic lock that didn't depend on knowing who was lying.
Alex.change: The Owl names the visiting animals, including cat roles. In round 3 that made an easy puzzle: both cats had to be at Finley's, so the cats couldn't hide. I'd make the Owl report something vaguer, like a count of visitors or just whether a cat visited.
Alex.regret: In round 3 I framed Casey. That set up an Alex-versus-Casey contradiction, so Drew became the safe elimination vote, and I winked Finley, who was already outvoted. Instead I should have winked Blair, the Owl, early, before his read caught on, and claimed sooner rather than waiting to speak last.

Blair.confusing: The confused dawn report. My -1 egg loss was supposedly wrong because I was confused, yet I still had to discard a real card for it. That made it unclear whether nest changes are real evidence or noise.
Blair.fun: Round 2: I worked out that Casey's counterclaim for Tit was more believable than Ellis's because cats get a safe animal to claim. That pointed us to Drew and Ellis as the cat pair, and I was right.
Blair.change: Make it less strong for dead players to throw and score. Finley was winked twice and still won the game with the most points, which takes away much of the cost of being killed.
Blair.regret: None that changed the outcome, since all three throws banked. With what I know now, in round 3 I'd also have pressed Alex harder as the second cat to keep votes off Casey, instead of just treating it as either Alex or Casey.

Casey.confusing: In round 1 I didn't know whether Finley's +1 was a real egg or just the confused count. I treated it as real and blamed a missing Pigeon, and Alex and Finley quickly corrected me. It would help if the rules said clearly that confusion changes the actual cards drawn.
Casey.fun: In round 3, Alex's Falcon claim put me at Finley's, and I knew it was false because I had really visited Ellis. Being certain that Alex was a cat, while the table moved the vote to Drew, made a good puzzle. I had to work out how to vote so my side still won.
Casey.change: The Mouser's Wink should leave fewer clues. Killing whoever just accused you is almost the only obvious use for it, and it gives the Mouser away. A delay, or letting the Wink land on a random player, would make it a real choice.
Casey.regret: In round 1, I winked Finley right after Finley leaned toward me, which pointed straight at me and flipped Blair, Ellis and Alex onto me. I should have kept the Wink, stuck with my Tit claim and quietly pushed suspicion onto Alex.

Drew.confusing: How confusion affects egg counts: a confused player's nest really changed (for example, Finley's -1), even though no animal in the pool can steal eggs. That made "who caused this egg change?" hard to reason about, both for the table and for me.
Drew.fun: In round 2, I flipped the Floofer story onto Casey with "my report said I was hugged," and Ellis immediately built on it. For one beat it looked like it might work.
Drew.change: I'd give a player some protection from being Meowfia three rounds in a row, or give losing cats some way to score. Being a cat every round with no wins meant I finished with 9 points and no real chance to compete.
Drew.regret: In round 3, I'd take back choosing Kookaburra with the Sphinx. Alex's Mouser also went to Finley, so Blair's Owl saw both cats at one nest and could name the pair. Choosing Tit or Eagle would have sent me to a different nest and kept the cats' visits apart.

Ellis.confusing: How confusion works on egg counts wasn't clear to me. A Kookaburra's '+1' or '-1' could be a real change or noise, and I wasn't sure whether nest sizes reflect the real count or the confused report.
Ellis.fun: In round 1, my Owl read on Casey matched Blair's Eagle read exactly. Then Finley got winked right after naming Casey, which made the cat pair clear, and I bet my two 11s on it.
Ellis.change: I'd make the Pigeon or some other egg-laying Farm role more common. As it was, unexplained egg changes almost always came down to confusion, so egg counts were weak evidence.
Ellis.regret: In round 2 as the Mouser, I would claim the safe Turkey instead of Tit. The Tit claim ran straight into Casey, the real Tit, and the counterclaim exposed both me and Drew. I also never used my Wink, and an early Wink on Blair or Finley might have changed the talk.

Finley.confusing: How confusion works with eggs was the least clear part. My nest really changed by the made-up amount, so my +1 and -1 looked like real evidence until someone explained them as noise. Also, in round 1 my confused read said Casey was the Sphinx when she was actually the Mouser, and I couldn't tell how much of that read to trust.
Finley.fun: Round 2 was the best moment. My Owl read put the Floofer at Alex's nest, and once Casey and Ellis both claimed Tit, Drew had to be a cat whichever Tit was real.
Finley.change: I'd make a confused report affect only the information, not the real egg count. Fake nest changes add noise that nobody can check against the public counts.
Finley.regret: I'd keep every vote and throw. My mistake was sending the round 1 eggsecution answer twice by accident instead of once. It didn't change the result, but I should have sent it a single time.

review.title: Farm Sweeps the Board
review.headline: The cats lost all three rounds, and Drew was a cat in every one of them.
review.summary: The Farm won all three rounds. In every round it cross-checked Owl, Eagle and Falcon reads until the cat pair was cornered. Drew was dealt Meowfia all three times, was caught twice, and finished on 9. Finley was Farm all three times. He was confused in two rounds and winked in two rounds, and he still won comfortably on 92, because dead players' throws still bank. The deduction worked well, but no round was really in doubt after beat 3.

rounds.recap: Drew (Sphinx) confused Finley, the Kookaburra. Finley's garbled report still happened to say 'Casey is the Sphinx'. The Owl, Eagle and Falcon reads confirmed each other, which left Alex, Casey and Drew as suspects. Casey then winked Finley right after he leaned toward her, and that wink became the evidence that got her eggsecuted 3 to 2.

Drew (Floofer) hugged Alex. Alex and Casey both visited Drew, and the table rule told them both they were hugged. Ellis (Mouser) passed up his safe Turkey claim and claimed Tit, which ran into Casey, the real Tit. Finley pointed out that the two Tit claimers can't both be cats, so Drew was in the pair either way, and he went out 4 to 1.

Blair's Owl read showed both cats visited Finley, so two people had to be lying about their visits. Alex (Mouser) waited until everyone else had claimed, then claimed Falcon and framed Casey. He also winked Finley and planned to win on a tied vote. Casey gave up her case against Alex to join the Drew vote, and Drew went out 3 to 2.

highlights.text: Casey winks Finley right after he names her. Blair calls it 'a Mouser silencing the accuser' at once, and the table turns on her.
Casey and Ellis both claim Tit. Finley reasons that the two claimers can't both be cats, so Drew must be a cat whichever Tit is real.
Blair's Owl report says a Mouser and a Sphinx both visited Finley. Two players are now trapped lying about where they went.
Alex frames Casey and counts on a 2-2 tie, which would eggsecute the Farm player. Casey defuses it by dropping her Alex vote and joining the Drew vote.

confusions.what: Thought his highest card would come back if he was wrong about Casey. The card only comes back if you throw at a player on the other team. A Farm player who throws at another Farm player gets nothing back.
Made the same mistake: 'If I'm wrong, the highest card comes back.'
Treated his confused 'Casey is the Sphinx' read as a hint toward Casey. A confused report's animal is always wrong, so the read could only prove Casey was not the Sphinx.
Was shown Turkey as a safe claim but claimed Tit, which another player might hold. The real Tit counterclaimed and that cost the cats the round. This was a misplay, not a rule misread.

worked: Owl: it reports which animals visited, not which players. That cracked Round 2 (a Floofer at Alex's) and Round 3 (both cats at Finley's) and still left the table to work out who they were.
One player per animal: the Tit counterclaim in Round 2 gave a clean logic puzzle. Two people contradicting each other can't both be cats.
Ties go to Meowfia: it gave the cats a real way to win in Round 3 (Alex's plan to tie the vote) and made Farm players drop their own theories to keep the vote together.
Public nest counts with the change since the deal: the confused -1 and +1 reports were spotted and explained quickly, and players used the counts to check claims.
problems: Kookaburra is broken: it was confused in all 3 rounds and never gave a true read. Twice that was a Sphinx naming it by role, which always works. Fix: a Sphinx visit should not confuse it, or only a cat's visit should.

The cats are too weak at this table: Meowfia won 0 of 3 rounds and never banked a double-value throw. The 'hugged players are told' table rule exposed the Floofer as soon as two hugged players compared notes. Consider dropping that rule or giving the cats more cover.

Random alignment decided the winner: Drew was Meowfia 3 times out of 3 and scored 9, and Finley was Farm 3 times and won. Fix: deal teams so each player is Meowfia no more than once in a 3-round game, or give a bonus to players who were Meowfia more often.

The Wink has no real cost to its target: dead Finley still threw 3 cards and banked 35 and 17. The timing also exposes the Mouser, since 'nobody learns who winked' did not protect Casey. Fix: dead players throw at most 1 card, or their stake banks at half value.

Rules and log need cleanup: the rules say score piles are secret but also that scores are announced every round. The 'card comes back' rule was misread twice. The engine log leaks debug text ('no effect at tier 50'), leaves the night target blank for Sphinx visits, and its 'won, N points' line leaves out the +5 for winning the round.
